ety.text: Unknown, rare in literary Latin. Perhaps from Gaulish or Germanic, ultimately either from Proto-Indo-European *bʰedʰh₂- (“to stab, dig”), or a separate root *bʰat- (“to hit”); ultimately onomatopoeic. Compare Welsh bathu (“beat”), Old English beadu (“battle”), and the latter half of Latin andabata, as well as perhaps Sanskrit भल्ल (bhalla, “arrowhead; missile”). Doublet of battō. Compare typologically Proto-Slavic *kopati (cognate with Latvian kapāt).
Derived from Beniamin (“Benjamin”) + -ītēs (“-ite”, adjective-forming suffix).
